backupMethod: Logical export via SELECT + sanitized SQL INSERT generation (postgres.js). pg_dump not available in environment.
restoreTarget: Separate schema 'restore_smoke_target' within the same Supabase dev project. NOT the live 'public' schema. This is a local smoke restore, not a managed disaster-recovery setup.

relationshipChecks.detail: 1 approvals resolve draft + have subject hash (expected 1)

limitations: This is a LOCAL SMOKE RESTORE into a separate schema within the same Supabase dev project, NOT a managed disaster-recovery setup.

pg_dump was not available in the environment; backup was captured via SELECT + sanitized SQL INSERT generation using postgres.js. A production backup should use pg_dump or Supabase's managed backup tool.
The restore target is a separate schema (restore_smoke_target), not a separate database/project. A production restore test should use a separate Supabase project or local PostgreSQL instance.
The restore schema tables have a simplified structure (no FKs, no enums, no CHECK constraints) — only the columns needed for smoke verification. A production restore must use the full schema.

Supabase Storage files are NOT included in this backup — only database rows. Storage backup is a separate concern (Contract 01: 'Back up or independently retain required Storage source/import files and metadata').
This does NOT prove production readiness. It proves the logical backup data can be loaded and relationships resolve.

Provider-managed backups (Supabase PITR) may supplement this process when the selected plan supports them. Free-tier managed-backup assumptions must not replace a demonstrated logical backup and restore test.
